description: The bar chart illustrates the perplexity of LLaMA1-7B on three different validation datasets—WikiText, PTB, and C4—under varying quantization bit settings (3, 4, 8, and 16 bits), comparing the performance of a uniform quantization approach (Uniform) against the proposed method (Ours). The vertical axis represents perplexity, with values ranging from 0 to 30 for WikiText and C4, and up to 420 for PTB, while the horizontal axis indicates the number of quantization bits. In all three datasets, the proposed method (Ours) consistently achieves lower perplexity than the Uniform method across all quantization bit levels. For WikiText, the Uniform method shows a perplexity of approximately 29.5 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 26.5 at 16 bits, while the Ours method ranges from about 21.5 to 18.5. In PTB, the Uniform method starts at a high perplexity of approximately 405 at 3 bits and decreases to around 310 at 16 bits, whereas the Ours method starts at about 250 and decreases to roughly 180. For C4, the Uniform method has a perplexity of approximately 29 at 3 bits, decreasing to about 25 at 16 bits, while the Ours method ranges from about 21 to 18. The results indicate that the proposed method maintains lower perplexity across all datasets and quantization levels, suggesting improved performance with less information loss compared to uniform quantization.
